subject: Culture
title: Indigenous Land and Sacred Sites
description: A quick, practical guide to Indigenous Land and Sacred Sites.

hook.text: Mount Rushmore was carved on the Six Grandfathers—a mountain sacred to the Lakota Sioux since before Columbus.

buildup.text: Colonial governments routinely built on indigenous sacred sites, treating them as empty real estate.

discovery.text: Uluru was closed to climbers in 2019 after decades of Aboriginal protest. Tourism had desecrated their sacred site.

twist.text: The US Supreme Court ruled in 1988 that logging on sacred Yurok land was legal because no single religion was affected.

climax.text: Western law struggles with sacred sites because it sees nature as property, not as a living entity with rights.

punchline.text: Ownership and sacredness speak different languages.
